categories.name: AI Agents
categories.description: Agent frameworks, multi-agent systems and autonomous workflows

analysis.why_trending: Growth is going to tools that give agents new abilities. vercel-labs/agent-desktop (+12120), cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+10695) and NVIDIA/auto-ontology (+10159) gained the most stars. Skill collections are also growing fast: mattpocock/skills has 319861★ (+9800), and claude-mem added +5130.
analysis.what_exists: There are skill repos from Anthropic, Matt Pocock and Cloudflare, accessibility-tree CLIs for browsers and desktop apps, and memory plugins like claude-mem. There are also large multi-agent setups such as Claude-Code-Game-Studios, which has 49 agents and 72 skills.
gaps: No way to test or score whether a skill actually improves agent output
Skills from different repos can conflict or duplicate each other, and nothing manages that
Hard to see what agents with desktop or VM access actually did
Multi-agent setups are hard to debug once they reach dozens of agents

ideas.title: Skill Bench
ideas.pitch: A harness that runs the same tasks with and without a skill and reports the difference in results. Skill authors and teams choosing skills would use it.
ideas.why_now: Skill repos like mattpocock/skills (+9800) and cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+10695) are growing faster than anyone can evaluate them.

ideas.title: Skill Lockfile
ideas.pitch: A CLI that installs skills from several repos, pins their versions and flags overlapping or conflicting instructions. Developers mixing skill packs would use it.
ideas.why_now: Developers now pull skills from several popular sources at once, including Anthropic, Matt Pocock and Cloudflare.

ideas.title: Agent Action Replay
ideas.pitch: A recorder that captures accessibility-tree actions from desktop and browser agents and lets users replay them step by step. Teams auditing computer-use agents would use it.
ideas.why_now: agent-desktop (+12120) and agent-browser are giving agents control of real apps.

categories.name: Developer Tools
categories.description: CLIs, terminals, editors, git tooling and productivity

analysis.why_trending: Rust CLIs built for agents lead this category: agent-desktop gained +12120 and worktrunk gained +2395. Worktree management and PR review (pr-agent, +1822) point to developers running several agents in parallel. sherlock (+4267) is still drawing strong interest.
analysis.what_exists: Tools here include worktrunk for Git worktrees, pr-agent for AI reviews, agent-autoloop for background agent tasks, and Concat, a video editor that can be scripted over MCP. Several new native Rust apps are also listed.
gaps: No dashboard showing which agent is working in which worktree
AI-written PRs are hard to tie back to the agent session that produced them
No simple check of whether a tool's claims are legitimate (for example, dsh-our-free-model's claim of free, unlimited model access with no API key)

ideas.title: Worktree Board
ideas.pitch: A terminal UI that shows each Git worktree with its branch, the agent running in it, its diff size and test status. Developers running parallel agents would use it.
ideas.why_now: worktrunk gained +2395 stars as people adopted parallel worktree workflows.

ideas.title: PR Provenance
ideas.pitch: A git hook plus a GitHub Action that attaches a summary of the agent session and its prompts to each PR. Reviewers using pr-agent-style tools would use it.
ideas.why_now: pr-agent (+1822) shows that AI review is becoming standard, but reviewers still lack context on how the code was written.

ideas.title: Repo Trust Check
ideas.pitch: A CLI that reviews a plugin repo before installation, checking its network calls, credential use and install scripts. Developers trying trending plugins would use it.
ideas.why_now: Trending plugins include ones making bold claims, such as dsh-our-free-model's free, unlimited frontier model access.

categories.name: AI Coding Tools
categories.description: Coding agents, code assistants, AI code review and generation

analysis.why_trending: Coding agents are being extended with design skills (hallmark +5987), memory (claude-mem +5130) and workflow tools like worktrunk (+2395) and pr-agent (+1822). magpie (33214★) shows developers want to switch the model behind each agent.
analysis.what_exists: magpie routes agents to different models, agent-autoloop runs agents in the background, and pr-agent reviews PRs. Several skill packs are also aimed at Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
gaps: No cost or quality comparison when switching models behind an agent
Background agents need better escalation and approval inboxes
Skills and memory don't carry over between Claude Code, Cursor and Codex

ideas.title: Model Swap Benchmarks
ideas.pitch: A runner that sends the same coding task to the same agent with different backend models and compares the diffs, test results and cost. Developers using magpie-style routing would use it.
ideas.why_now: magpie (33214★) makes model swapping easy but doesn't show the tradeoffs.

ideas.title: Agent Approval Inbox
ideas.pitch: A mobile or web inbox that collects decision cards from background coding agents in one place. Solo developers running agent-autoloop would use it.
ideas.why_now: agent-autoloop (4306★) and dsh-Go point to agents that run unattended and only ask for decisions when needed.

ideas.title: Cross-Agent Skill Sync
ideas.pitch: A converter that keeps skills and rules files in sync across Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Teams using more than one agent would use it.
ideas.why_now: hallmark already targets all three agents, which shows demand for working across them.

categories.name: Web & App Frameworks
categories.description: Frontend, full-stack and mobile frameworks and UI kits

analysis.why_trending: Web frameworks are being redesigned with agents as users. meta/astryx (+3278) is a design system built for agents, and Scrapling (+8226) is a scraping framework. Open alternatives to Grok Bot are also rising, such as OpenMausBot (+1587) and rakazo (+143).
analysis.what_exists: Options include agent-friendly design systems (astryx), native UI frameworks (rune), scrapers (Scrapling) and auto-generated news sites (AIHOT). There are also mobile clients for agent harnesses, such as dsh-Go.
gaps: No way to check whether agent-generated UI actually follows a design system
Few templates for web front ends that let people supervise sandboxed bots
Few mobile-first interfaces for controlling agents

ideas.title: Design System Linter for Agents
ideas.pitch: A CI check that flags components and tokens in agent-written UI that don't come from astryx or another chosen design system. Frontend teams using coding agents would use it.
ideas.why_now: astryx (+3278) is designed to work with agents, but nothing checks whether agents actually follow it.

ideas.title: Sandbox Bot Console Kit
ideas.pitch: A React starter app that streams the screen, logs and approval prompts from a bot's VM or sandbox. Builders of OpenMausBot or rakazo deployments would use it.
ideas.why_now: Open Grok Bot alternatives like OpenMausBot (+1587) need front ends.

ideas.title: Source-to-Digest Starter
ideas.pitch: A small template that uses Scrapling to pull from configured sources and publishes a static daily digest site. Niche communities and students would use it.
ideas.why_now: Scrapling (+8226) and AIHOT (10100★) show demand for automated topic sites.

categories.name: LLM Apps & RAG
categories.description: Chat apps, RAG pipelines, prompt tooling and vector search

analysis.why_trending: Users want output that doesn't look AI-generated and agents that remember context. hallmark (+5987) and unslop target generic AI design, and claude-mem (+5130) handles memory. Interest in structured reasoning over data also appears in auto-ontology (+10159).
analysis.what_exists: Projects include design skills (hallmark, unslop), session memory (claude-mem), tutoring agents (DeepTutor), stock analysis pipelines and Claude quickstarts.
gaps: No objective way to measure whether a design looks AI-generated
Memory plugins don't let users inspect or edit what was stored
Few ways to connect ontology layers to existing RAG stacks

ideas.title: Slop Score
ideas.pitch: A tool that screenshots a UI and scores it on common AI-generated design patterns, so users can compare results before and after applying hallmark or unslop. Designers and agent users would use it.
ideas.why_now: hallmark (+5987) and unslop (12808★) show demand, but there is no way to measure their effect.

ideas.title: Memory Inspector
ideas.pitch: A local UI for browsing, editing and deleting the compressed sessions stored by claude-mem-style plugins. Heavy agent users would use it.
ideas.why_now: claude-mem reached 115434★ (+5130), so a lot of memory is being stored without a way to review it.

ideas.title: Ontology-to-RAG Adapter
ideas.pitch: A library that adds results from an auto-ontology graph to vector search retrieval. RAG builders would use it.
ideas.why_now: auto-ontology gained +10159 stars quickly but has no RAG integrations.

categories.name: Infra, Self-hosting & Security
categories.description: DevOps, databases, self-hosted apps and security tools

analysis.why_trending: Security work is moving into agents: cloudflare/security-audit-skill gained +10695. Sandboxes for agents are also active (OpenSandbox +168, OpenMausBot +1587), and OSINT tools like sherlock (+4267) keep growing.
analysis.what_exists: There are agent sandbox runtimes (OpenSandbox), network monitors (sniffnet), Android privacy auditors (NOIR), bloatware removers (cleanyourtv) and agent-run audit skills.
gaps: Machine-readable audit findings don't feed into existing issue trackers or SARIF dashboards
Agent sandboxes don't show which network destinations an agent contacts
No guidance on responsible use of OSINT username searches

ideas.title: Audit Findings Bridge
ideas.pitch: A converter that turns security-audit-skill output into SARIF and GitHub issues, and removes duplicates across runs. Security engineers would use it.
ideas.why_now: cloudflare/security-audit-skill (+10695) produces machine-readable findings, but they have nowhere standard to go.

ideas.title: Sandbox Egress Monitor
ideas.pitch: A sniffnet-style view of the network traffic leaving an OpenSandbox or bot VM, with allow-list alerts. Teams self-hosting agents would use it.
ideas.why_now: Agent sandboxes (OpenSandbox, OpenMausBot) are trending alongside network monitoring (sniffnet, 42241★).

ideas.title: Self Exposure Check
ideas.pitch: A privacy tool that runs only on your own username or device and suggests cleanup steps, combining username searches with NOIR-style app audits. Privacy-minded individuals would use it.
ideas.why_now: sherlock (+4267) and NOIR show interest in exposure tools, and this version is aimed at self-defense.

categories.name: MCP Tooling
categories.description: Model Context Protocol servers, clients and agent tool integrations

analysis.why_trending: Creative desktop apps are shipping with MCP built in, such as Concat for video and SolidCraft for CAD. Agent control of apps is also growing fast (agent-desktop +12120, Scrapling +8226), and Anthropic now runs an official plugin directory (46648★).
analysis.what_exists: There are MCP-scriptable creative apps, Anthropic's official plugin directory and learning resources like ai-engineering-from-scratch. There are also tools like BLA that try to resist AI reverse-engineering.
gaps: No standard test suite for MCP servers built into apps
Long-running creative MCP operations have no undo or preview
Hard to find MCP-enabled apps outside the official directory

ideas.title: MCP Conformance Tester
ideas.pitch: A CLI that checks an MCP server's schemas, error handling and timeouts. Developers adding MCP to apps like Concat or SolidCraft would use it.
ideas.why_now: Creative apps such as Concat and SolidCraft are now shipping MCP support.

ideas.title: MCP Dry-Run Proxy
ideas.pitch: A proxy that logs tool calls, previews them and lets users roll back destructive calls before they reach the app. Creators who give agents control of editors would use it.
ideas.why_now: Video and CAD tools like Concat and SolidCraft let agents edit project files directly.

ideas.title: MCP App Index
ideas.pitch: A searchable list of desktop apps that support MCP, with their capabilities and setup snippets. Agent users would use it.
ideas.why_now: The official plugin directory has 46648★, but app-embedded MCP servers are spread across many repos.

categories.name: Browser Agents
categories.description: Tools that automate browser workflows and scrape the web

analysis.why_trending: Scrapling (+8226) leads this category, and accessibility-tree browsing (agent-browser +916) is maturing. New projects give each agent its own browser or computer with audit trails, such as OpenBot, lcu and BrowserKitten.
analysis.what_exists: Options include scraping frameworks, headless browsers built for agents (ff-ruyijs), side-panel agents in the user's own browser (BrowserKitten) and AI crawler analytics (GEOInflow). There are also OSINT tools like maigret.
gaps: Agent browsing traces aren't reusable as deterministic scripts
Sites can't easily tell which agents are visiting them
No shared benchmark across agent browsers

ideas.title: Trace to Script
ideas.pitch: A tool that turns a recorded agent-browser session into a repeatable Playwright or Scrapling script. Teams automating recurring tasks would use it.
ideas.why_now: agent-browser (48584★) and Scrapling (+8226) are both growing, and this connects them.

ideas.title: Agent Browser Bench
ideas.pitch: A suite of local test sites for comparing headless agent browsers on accuracy and speed. Tool authors and researchers would use it.
ideas.why_now: Several agent browsers appeared at the same time, including ff-ruyijs, agent-browser and BrowserKitten.

ideas.title: Agent Visitor Policy
ideas.pitch: Middleware that detects agent traffic and applies site rules, building on GEOInflow-style analytics. Site owners would use it.
ideas.why_now: More agent browsing means site owners need visibility, as GEOInflow shows.
